page: Microsoft Azure D64s_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture, running on Microsoft Hyper-V. The instance is powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at a base frequency of 2.8 GHz, supplying 64 dedicated vCPUs distributed across 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Cache hierarchy includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of shared L3 cache, with hardware instruction support for AVX, AVX-512, VNNI, VAES, and SHA extensions.

System memory is provisioned at 256.0 GB, maintaining a balanced ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance is diskless, containing zero bundled local storage, which necessitates the attachment of external block volumes with Premium Storage support for persistence. The instance also features zero GPU accelerators. In memory subsystem benchmarks, the host delivered strong uncached large-block throughput, achieving 283.92 GB/sec in sequential read operations and 136.39 GB/sec in write operations.

Benchmark results demonstrate a clear separation between single-thread and multi-thread capabilities. While single-core scores in Geekbench and stress-ng sit within the median performance bracket, multi-threaded tests register in the top quartile. PassMark CPU scores, software compilation tasks with Clang, ray tracing, static web serving throughput of 50.18 GB/sec, and database operations all perform in the upper 25 percent. Conversely, CPU-based LLM inference rates remain average across model sizes.

The D64s_v5 provides a dense compute and memory footprint without the overhead of local ephemeral disks, making it cost-efficient for architectures designed around centralized network storage. The lack of integrated storage requires infrastructure designers to evaluate network storage latency and bandwidth against application needs. The server is suited for enterprise relational databases, large-scale CI/CD build environments, and high-concurrency web serving infrastructure.
description: Microsoft Azure D64s_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine delivering 64 dedicated vCPUs and 256.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a balanced 4.0 GB per vCPU ratio. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz on Microsoft Hyper-V, the system incorporates 32 physical cores, 48 MB of L3 cache, and advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and VNNI. The instance carries no bundled local storage or GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage architectures. Benchmark data reveals strong parallel compute capabilities, logging upper-quartile results in PassMark multi-core evaluations, software compilation, database operations, and large-block memory read bandwidth reaching 283.92 GB/sec. Single-core throughput and CPU-based LLM generation remain within median percentiles. This configuration is engineered for high-concurrency enterprise workloads, distributed database backends, software compilation pipelines, and container hosts.
